proposals.summary: Add the strongest probe: reassign a terminal bus to the busiest route when queue_ratio_other >= 6.67, keeping the existing queue-relief dispatch.
proposals.rationale: The champion leaves 1,088 riders behind on r3 and 206 waiting at Old Main, while r2/r1 terminals can sit with idle buses. The probe that reassigns a terminal bus to the busiest route when queue_ratio_other >= 6.67 is the only measured change above 1% (-2.6%), directly moving capacity toward the most-pressured route. Keeping queue-relief-dispatch preserves the existing fast dispatch behavior, and the high 6.67 ratio guard prevents pulling r2 buses off Central transfers except in extreme imbalance. Changes: Add terminal rule reassigning to busiest when queue_ratio_other >= 6.67 (priority 30); Keep queue-relief-dispatch and even-headway unchanged.

proposals.summary: Add the supported terminal reassign-to-busiest rule (queue_ratio_other >= 6.67) and move one bus from the least-pressured route r1 to the most-pressured r3.
proposals.rationale: The strongest probe (-2.6%) reassigns a bus to the busiest route when another route's queue dwarfs this one, directly attacking the r3 Old Main/Stadium Station left-behinds (1,088) and the r2 Central transfer misses (494). The second probe (-1.4%) moves a bus r1->r3, matching the pressure ranking (r3 > r2 > r1) and the flagged unused capacity on r1; r1 keeps 1 bus so service stays intact. Both changes are allocation-focused and independently supported by the probes. Changes: Add bus_at_terminal rule reassign-to-busiest when queue_ratio_other >= 6.67; Change allocation from 2/2/2 to 1/2/3 (move one bus r1 -> r3).

proposals.summary: Add a guarded terminal reassign rule that sends a bus to the busiest route only when an r3/r1-style queue imbalance is extreme, keeping it from pulling r2 off Central transfers.
proposals.rationale: The strongest probe (reassign to busiest when queue_ratio_other >= 6.67, -2.6%) attacks the dominant finding: 206 riders left behind for r3 at Old Main and 72 at Stadium Station, plus r2 Central queues. Untuned, that rule can strip r2 buses from Central, so I guard it to fire only at extreme imbalance and only outside the event window, and combine it with a modest bus shift from the least-pressured route r1 to the most-pressured r3 (probe -1.4%). Together these add capacity where riders are actually stranded without touching the transfer-critical r2 allocation. Changes: +terminal rule reassign-to-busiest when queue_ratio_other>=6.67 & route_queue<20 & event_in_s<0, priority 30; move 1 bus r1->r3 (allocation 1/2/3).
